> Use Pi freely. Each exercise ends with a **Part 3 — Check the agent**. That
> part is the point: the skill we are building is catching a confident wrong
> answer, not avoiding the agent.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

data_dir <- "data/2-workshop2/instructional_dataset"

metadata <- read_csv(here(data_dir, "01_metadata.csv"))
species  <- read_csv(here(data_dir, "02_microbiome_counts.csv"))    # 220 species  x 471 samples
genes    <- read_csv(here(data_dir, "04_rnaseq_counts.csv.gz"))     # 14,226 genes x 471 samples
taxonomy <- read_csv(here(data_dir, "03_microbiome_taxonomy.csv"))
```


## Part 2 — Build

```{r}
# step 1: check the shapes line up with the metadata.
# The first column of each count table is the feature name. Every other column
# is a sample.
dim(species)
dim(genes)

# sample_ids in the metadata that have no column in the count table.
# Both should come back empty.
metadata |> filter(!sample_id %in% names(species))
metadata |> filter(!sample_id %in% names(genes))
```

```{r}
# step 2: reshape each table so it has one row per feature per sample.
species_long <- species |>
  pivot_longer(-taxon, names_to = "sample_id", values_to = "count")

# genes_long <- genes |> ...

```

```{r}
# step 2, continued: the four per-sample summaries, for `species_long` first.
# library_size, features_detected, zero_fraction, top_feature_share
#
# species_long |>
#   group_by(sample_id) |>
#   summarise(library_size = sum(count), ...)

```

```{r}
# step 3: do the same for `genes_long`, then stack the two with bind_rows() so
# you end up with one data frame that has a `table` column saying "species" or
# "genes".

```

```{r}

```

```{r}

# Then the Spearman correlation for each table:
#   cor(library_size, features_detected, method = "spearman")
# How many extra features does the trend actually amount to?

```

```{r}

# down to that sample and look at its counts.

```

```{r}

#   mutate(p = count / sum(count)) |>
#   filter(p > 0) |>
#   summarise(shannon   = -sum(p * log(p)),
#             effective = exp(shannon))
```
